newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Apartheid rich should give to race victims - ANC.
newsitem.headline: Apartheid rich should give to race victims - ANC.

text.p: South Africans who gained from apartheid should make voluntary reparations to those who suffered under it, Deputy President Thabo Mbeki said on Tuesday.

"There were people who benefited directly from this huge, gross humans rights abuse, this crime against humanity," Mbeki told reporters after a formal African National Congress presentation to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission.

As part of its mandate to heal the wounds of apartheid, the commission has powers to award financial or other help to victims of apartheid or families of those who died in the struggle to end white domination.
Asked if he was referring to corporations like Anglo American, Mbeki replied: "You are going to find resistance to a straight answer to this straight question."
But he said the ANC proposal, now in the hands of the truth commission, was not for a reparations tax on the wealthy.
"Those who have, those who were not deprived, who in a sense have something to lose, I think will find it in their interest...as part of the process of ensuring greater stability," Mbeki said.

"If the message can come across to the entirety of South African society, so that the inhabitants of Houghton -- including Nelson Mandela -- can say 'Why don't we have a quick whip round among ourselves, let's build a school, let's do something to inspire the population as a whole."
Houghton, where President Mandela has his private home, is one of Johannesburg's most affluent suburbs.
Mbeki said he preferred this approach to one that said "let's look at your profit returns and tax returns and so on to see to what extent you benefited from apartheid".
